story.value: Thulium is named after Thule, the earliest name for Scandinavia.
Thulium was discovered by the Swedish chemist Per Theodor Cleve in 1879.
Thulium was first isolated by the American chemist Charles James in 1911.

uses.value: One of thulium's isotopes could be used as a radiation source for portable X-ray machines.
Natural thulium has possible use in ferrites, which are ceramic magnetic materials used in microwave equipment.
Natural thulium can be used for doping fiber lasers.
